lessons.title: ATLAS purpose, users, and terminology
objectives: Explain the purpose of ATLAS and who uses it
Distinguish the Atlas product name from Almanac naming in code
lessons.starterQuestion: What is ATLAS, who uses it, and why does its source code say Almanac?

assessment.question: Explain ATLAS to a new teammate, including its users and the Atlas/Almanac naming difference.
requiredConcepts: ATLAS supports service repair workflows for Trimble products
Authorized service technicians use the desktop application
Atlas is the product name while Almanac remains in source or assembly naming

lessons.title: Desktop installation, startup, and navigation
objectives: Identify installed components and startup dependencies
Locate Product Details, My Service Cases, Dashboard, Settings, Help, and About

sections: What Atlas does in the product

lessons.starterQuestion: What must be installed before Atlas starts, and where does a technician begin?

assessment.question: Describe Atlas startup dependencies and the main desktop navigation areas.
requiredConcepts: The installed system includes Atlas, License Activation, Reset Almanac Offline, and local MongoDB
Startup requires valid local licensing and authorizations and a running MongoDB service
Product Details identifies the unit and starts repair work; My Service Cases lists technician cases
Dashboard embeds related web views while Settings, Help, and About provide supporting functions

lessons.title: Identity, Atlas seats, activation, and authorizations
objectives: Distinguish authentication, application licensing, and product authorization
Explain activation operations and full external versus collimator capabilities
lessons.starterQuestion: Why can a successful sign-in still leave Atlas unavailable or a feature restricted?

assessment.question: Explain the difference between signing in, licensing Atlas, and being authorized for a product.
requiredConcepts: Trimble Identity sign-in is distinct from application-seat licensing and product authorizations
License Activation uses OData and writes local license and authorization XML consumed by desktop startup
Full external and collimator licenses expose different capabilities rather than the same repair workflow

lessons.title: The technician workflow
objectives: Describe the main stages of a technician visit
Explain why repair activity is captured against a service case

sections: What Atlas does in the product

lessons.starterQuestion: What happens from identifying an instrument to completing its service case?

assessment.question: Describe a typical technician visit and explain the role of the service case.
requiredConcepts: Identify the instrument and review relevant product, warranty, history, or bulletin context
Open or create a service case to capture the visit's repair activity
Perform service operations and save their results against the case before completion

lessons.title: Service-case workspace, results, and reports
objectives: Distinguish product-level context from the open service-case workspace
Explain how operations, parts, bulletins, and reports relate to the case

sections: Product Details and the service case page

lessons.starterQuestion: What belongs to Product Details, what belongs to a service case, and how are reports produced?

assessment.question: Explain how a technician records repair work and obtains the applicable case reports.
requiredConcepts: Product Details provides unit context while the service case captures the repair visit
The case records operations, parts, and applied bulletins through its workspace and task list
Report availability depends on recorded work and report-specific conditions, and generation requires network

lessons.title: Desktop manuals, bulletins, downloads, and instrument constants
objectives: Locate desktop product manuals, bulletins, downloads, and instrument-constant operations
Distinguish reading a bulletin from recording its application on a case

sections: What Atlas does in the product
Product Details and the service case page

lessons.starterQuestion: Where does Atlas desktop expose manuals, bulletins, downloads, and instrument constants?

assessment.question: Explain where service content appears and why viewing a bulletin is not the same as applying it.
requiredConcepts: Atlas provides relevant product content and feature-gated downloads or instrument-constant operations
Desktop service manuals are product-level rather than a service-case accordion
A bulletin used for its warranty window must be applied on the task list, not merely viewed

lessons.title: Detectors, service operations, and the Almanac API
objectives: Distinguish detectors from service operations
Explain documented plugin delivery, mapping, execution, and results
lessons.starterQuestion: How does an instrument-specific detector or operation become available inside Atlas?

assessment.question: Explain how Atlas discovers an instrument and runs its mapped service operations.
requiredConcepts: Detectors identify instruments while service operations perform device work
Atlas hosts Windows plugin DLLs or EXEs through the Almanac API
Installer binaries and Portal product-model mappings must align, and sync distributes the metadata
Plugin events or results are mapped into case results including pass or fail

lessons.title: DWCR, warranty exceptions, and internal Service-Support
objectives: Distinguish external warranty claims from internal repair-assistance requests
Explain the documented claim gates and case-completion outcomes
lessons.starterQuestion: How do DWCR and Service-Support differ in eligibility, destination, and case outcome?

assessment.question: Compare DWCR with Service-Support, including a documented warranty-exception path.
requiredConcepts: DWCR is an online MTP warranty claim for eligible full external technicians, and success completes the Atlas case
A documented exception can use an applied mandatory bulletin within its grace window or a selected previous closed repair case
DWCR submission goes directly to MTP; OData stores the claim row rather than submitting the claim
Internal Service-Support creates a Salesforce repair-assistance case, requires network, and neither creates a DWCR nor completes the Atlas case

lessons.title: BCS sites, calibration, monitoring, and approval
objectives: Explain where BCS runs and who can launch it
Describe the calibration-site workflow and its backend
lessons.starterQuestion: What does BCS calibrate, who can launch it, and where does its data go?

assessment.question: Describe a service provider's BCS workflow and distinguish it from ordinary case work.
requiredConcepts: BCS launches online from Atlas Settings for service-provider companies and is not a service-case screen
SX sites use prism or DR targets while X sites use spheres
The workflow covers sites, measurements, monitoring, and calibration approval
BCS stores data through eAtlas BCS APIs into Atlas SQL rather than using OData for BCS data

lessons.title: BCS notification levels, blockage, and failsafe
objectives: Distinguish monitoring reminders from calibration levels
Explain documented Level 3 case-opening blockage and exceptions
lessons.starterQuestion: When does BCS move from a reminder to blocking case creation or opening?

assessment.question: Explain a Level 3 BCS alert, its effect on service-case access, and the role of failsafe.
requiredConcepts: Calibration levels and monitoring reminders are separate notification tracks
The daily SQL procedure generates active rows that desktop consumes for alerts and restrictions
Level 3 can block create or open for affected X or SX product families
Documented failsafe exemptions or another valid local site can affect blockage; an alert alone does not establish every case is blocked

lessons.title: Desktop repair assistant: availability and product context
objectives: Explain the documented conditions for showing the repair assistant
Describe product and manual context without introducing ingestion implementation
lessons.starterQuestion: When does the repair assistant appear, and what product context does it receive?

assessment.question: Explain why the desktop repair assistant may be unavailable and what context it receives.
requiredConcepts: Availability depends on the user acknowledgment/enabled flag and applicable product, manual, serial-status, and support-date conditions
The assistant receives the current product model and classified service-manual filenames
Changing the product closes the prior session, while the same model can reuse its window
The product repair assistant is distinct from this onboarding tutor

lessons.title: Local MongoDB, offline limits, and synchronization
objectives: Explain local and server responsibilities during offline work
Distinguish cached repair activity from actions that require network
lessons.starterQuestion: What can a technician do offline, and what must wait for connectivity?

assessment.question: Explain what happens when connectivity drops during a repair after a successful Force Sync.
requiredConcepts: Previously synchronized data and repair changes are held in local MongoDB
Cached case editing can continue and local changes synchronize through OData when connectivity returns
Case completion, DWCR submission, report generation, Service-Support submission, and synchronization require network

lessons.title: Installed components, recovery risks, and environment boundaries
objectives: Identify installed Atlas components and documented startup dependencies
Distinguish local database reset from internal environment switching and their risks
lessons.starterQuestion: What does Atlas install, and how do reset and environment switching differ?

assessment.question: Explain installed startup dependencies and compare local reset with environment switching safely.
requiredConcepts: The installed system includes Atlas, License Activation, Reset Almanac Offline, and local MongoDB
Startup depends on valid local licensing and authorizations and a running MongoDB service
Reset drops local data, risks unsynchronized work, preserves license files, and requires later sync to rebuild
Environment Switch is internal-only and changes endpoint overlays, clears license/authorization files, and drops local data; field technician installs stay on production
The available documentation does not establish a complete installer build or deployment procedure

lessons.title: eAtlas purpose, users, sign-in, and desktop differences
objectives: Explain who uses eAtlas and how users sign in
Contrast browser management/content work with desktop instrument repair

sections: What Atlas does in the product

lessons.starterQuestion: Who uses eAtlas, how do they sign in, and how does it differ from Atlas desktop?

assessment.question: Introduce eAtlas to a technician who already knows Atlas desktop.
requiredConcepts: eAtlas is a browser application for service managers and other authorized company users
Sign-in uses Trimble Identity rather than the Almanac OData session token
Web work includes company cases, licenses, assignment, and content; desktop hosts instrument repair and Windows operations
Atlas can embed eAtlas Dashboard views, but the web application does not replace desktop instrument operations

lessons.title: eAtlas manager workflow and case assignment
objectives: Explain company-level case and license visibility
Describe how manager assignment reaches the technician
lessons.starterQuestion: How does assigning a case in eAtlas affect the technician's Atlas case list?

assessment.question: Describe a manager assigning a company case and explain how the technician sees that assignment.
requiredConcepts: eAtlas provides company service-case views and assignment for authorized users
Assignment updates the shared Atlas SQL case data and becomes visible on desktop load or sync
Assignment can be training-restricted, and OData preserves manager assignment during desktop updates

lessons.title: eAtlas content, company licenses, users, roles, and authorizations
objectives: Locate web service content and company administration surfaces
Distinguish web visibility from desktop activation and recorded case work
lessons.starterQuestion: What content and administration features does eAtlas provide beyond case assignment?

assessment.question: Describe eAtlas content and company administration and contrast them with desktop actions.
requiredConcepts: Web content includes manuals, bulletins, general service information, downloads, labor time guidance, and instrument constants
Company surfaces include license visibility, user administration, roles, and product/training authorizations
Available content and operations depend on modules, roles, and applicable authorization rather than universal access
Viewing licenses on the web is not desktop machine activation, and viewing a bulletin does not record its application on a repair case

lessons.title: ATLAS, OData, and eATLAS responsibilities
objectives: Distinguish desktop, primary backend, and web application responsibilities
Explain the role of local MongoDB and the shared SQL catalog

sections: What Atlas does in the product

lessons.starterQuestion: How do ATLAS desktop, OData, eATLAS, local MongoDB, and SQL fit together?

assessment.question: Explain the responsibilities of ATLAS desktop, OData, and eATLAS, including where local and shared data fit.
requiredConcepts: ATLAS desktop supports technician repair workflows
OData is the primary desktop backend
eATLAS serves service managers and also provides embedded views or selected secondary desktop APIs
Local MongoDB supports offline work
OData and eATLAS use the same Atlas SQL catalog

lessons.title: Salesforce/TWoD master data and desktop distribution
objectives: Identify the upstream owner of catalog and organization data
Trace incremental master-data distribution to Atlas clients
lessons.starterQuestion: Where does Atlas catalog data originate, and how does it reach a technician PC?

assessment.question: Trace a product-catalog update from its upstream source to the desktop.
requiredConcepts: Salesforce/TWoD supplies master data rather than Atlas creating the catalog itself
The daily incremental sync writes Atlas SQL using per-domain synchronization watermarks
OData distributes the resulting catalog through desktop sync into local MongoDB
Master-data ingest and desktop transaction synchronization are different stages

lessons.title: EMS back-office flow for Atlas application seats
objectives: Trace purchased external seats from Oracle through EMS to Atlas activation
Distinguish current external-seat provisioning from legacy and internal licensing
lessons.starterQuestion: How does a purchased Atlas seat become an activation code and a working desktop license?

assessment.question: Trace the external Atlas-seat flow and distinguish it from internal and instrument licensing.
requiredConcepts: Oracle orders reach EMS entitlements through middleware
Atlas EMS integration creates an activation code and Atlas SQL records, while OData licensing provisions or binds the external seat
License Activation obtains signed local license/authorization files; EMS is not the desktop UI
New purchased external seats use EMS, Poseidon is legacy, and internal licenses are Atlas-issued
These are Atlas application seats rather than temporary instrument service keys

lessons.title: Temporary instrument service licenses
objectives: Separate instrument service keys from Atlas application seats
Explain the authorization and OKWS responsibility boundaries

sections: Why it exists (Hardware as a Service)
What this service does vs what it does not

lessons.starterQuestion: How does an instrument service license differ from the license needed to run Atlas?

assessment.question: Describe the temporary instrument service-license flow and distinguish it from EMS seats.
requiredConcepts: Instrument service licenses enable temporary device service capabilities or controlled serial changes, not Atlas desktop seats
License Generator Service checks identity and product authorization and forwards requests to OKWS
OKWS issues the key; Atlas or its plugin applies it rather than inventing the key
The instrument returns to its purchased configuration after the temporary service override

lessons.title: Instrument constants: upload, comparison, and archive
objectives: Explain the separate watcher and comparer responsibilities
Describe success and mismatch outcomes without confusing constants with catalog data
lessons.starterQuestion: Why are both File System Watcher and File Comparer needed for instrument constants?

assessment.question: Trace an instrument-constant file from the share through verification and describe a mismatch.
requiredConcepts: Watcher maps files with sorting rules, uploads through eAtlas to S3, and moves successes to Uploaded
Comparer runs afterward, downloads the cloud copy, and compares file bytes
Matches move to Archived while mismatches remain in Uploaded with logging and notification
Instrument-constant file processing is distinct from Salesforce master-data ingest

lessons.title: Service-bulletin email notifications
objectives: Explain the dependency on TWoD bulletin ingest
Describe recipient filtering and duplicate-mail tracking
lessons.starterQuestion: Why might a new bulletin appear in Atlas but not produce an email for every user?

assessment.question: Explain how the bulletin mailer chooses new content and eligible recipients.
requiredConcepts: The mailer reads SQL notifications after TWoD ingest rather than fetching Salesforce itself
Recipient selection depends on active subscription and applicable company/product authorization
Watermarks and per-user mailing status identify new work and avoid already-sent bulletins
Email delivery is separate from desktop visibility, BCS alerts, and AI knowledge-base synchronization

lessons.title: Manual and bulletin ingestion for the repair assistant
objectives: Distinguish manual-upload and bulletin-ingest triggers
Explain asynchronous knowledge synchronization and desktop assistant context
lessons.starterQuestion: How do manuals and bulletins reach the repair assistant, and why can updates take time?

assessment.question: Compare manual and bulletin synchronization and explain their relationship to desktop AI chat.
requiredConcepts: Successful manual create or replace in eAtlas triggers asynchronous manual ingest
Bulletins synchronize after TWoD into a separate library, including removal of deactivated bulletins
Synchronization is eventually consistent, and manual deletion is not wired from eAtlas
Desktop assistant context includes the product model and manual filenames; the product repair assistant is not the onboarding tutor

lessons.title: Atlas Global Service and external consumers
objectives: Distinguish Global Service from the desktop backend
Explain its documented external-team use cases without generalizing access rules
lessons.starterQuestion: Why does Atlas Global Service exist alongside OData and eAtlas?

assessment.question: Explain Global Service consumers and distinguish its warranty lookup from claim submission.
requiredConcepts: Global Service gives other Trimble teams focused access to Atlas facts rather than serving the desktop repair workflow
Its documented use cases include calibration PDFs, recent closed-case lookup, and a Sentinel user/open-case check
The warranty endpoint looks up case facts; it does not submit DWCR or issue instrument service keys
The documentation describes route-specific authentication rather than a uniform TID requirement for every endpoint

lessons.title: Capstone: trace a repair and investigate a failure with repository evidence
objectives: Connect the product journey to documented service and data boundaries
Distinguish supported explanations from hypotheses and missing evidence
lessons.starterQuestion: How would you explain a repair end to end and investigate a blocked step using documentation and read-only source code?

assessment.question: Trace an illustrative repair across desktop, local and shared stores, and services. Explain a blocked step with repository evidence and one explicit evidence gap.
requiredConcepts: The repair journey connects instrument identification, case activity, and an eligible completion or claim path
The trace distinguishes local MongoDB, primary OData, eAtlas/shared SQL, and direct MTP DWCR submission
A network-loss or BCS Level 3 example explains the applicable documented restriction without claiming a proven runtime diagnosis
The explanation cites document sections and any inspected code paths or symbols, labels hypotheses, identifies missing evidence, and does not modify or execute product code or access external systems
